title: The Reasons We Borrow
fact_notes: 架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査、統計、観測、制度、実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: During a fictional philosophy seminar, several students discover that they have chosen the same position on a difficult question for remarkably different reasons.
sentences.ja: 架空の哲学ゼミで複数の学生は難しい問いに対して驚くほど異なる理由から同じ立場を選んだと知る。

sentences.en: One explains that the position follows from a principle that she has considered carefully, while another admits that he initially adopted it because a person he admired had expressed a similar opinion.
sentences.ja: 一人は慎重に検討した原則からその立場が導かれると説明し、別の一人は尊敬する人物が同様の意見を述べたため当初採用したと認める。

sentences.en: A third student says that the conclusion simply seemed reasonable to her, although she cannot immediately identify the experiences or assumptions that might have made it appear so convincing.
sentences.ja: 三人目は結論が単に合理的に思えたと言うが、説得的に感じさせた経験や前提をすぐ特定できない。

sentences.en: Their instructor asks whether these differences concern only the history of their beliefs or also the strength of the arguments that they are now prepared to offer in support of them.
sentences.ja: 教員はこれらの違いが信念の来歴だけに関わるのか、現在支持のため提示できる論拠の強さにも関わるのか問う。

sentences.en: The class distinguishes the origin of a belief from the justification that a person can provide for continuing to hold it after examining relevant objections.
sentences.ja: 学生は信念の起源と関連する反論を検討した後も保持するため提示できる正当化を区別する。

sentences.en: Someone may have encountered a useful idea through an unreliable source and subsequently discovered independent evidence that provides a more convincing basis for accepting it.
sentences.ja: 信頼できない情報源で有益な考えに出会い、その後受け入れるためのより説得的な基盤となる独立した証拠を発見する人もいるかもしれない。

sentences.en: Conversely, a person who initially acquired a belief from a respected specialist might continue defending it long after the circumstances that originally justified it have changed.
sentences.ja: 逆に尊敬する専門家から当初信念を得た人も元の正当化事情が変わってかなりたった後まで擁護を続けるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The instructor therefore cautions against evaluating an argument exclusively by investigating the circumstances under which someone first encountered its conclusion.
sentences.ja: そこで教員は最初に結論に出会った事情を調べるだけで論拠を評価することに注意を促す。

sentences.en: However, the students also discuss why the social history of a belief can remain relevant when people attempt to assess their own reasoning.
sentences.ja: しかし学生は自らの推論を評価する際に信念の社会的来歴が依然関連し得る理由も議論する。

sentences.en: Someone who feels a strong obligation to defend the views of a particular community may find it difficult to examine an objection that would otherwise deserve considerable attention.
sentences.ja: 特定共同体の見解を守る強い義務を感じる人はそうでなければ十分注意に値する反論を検討しにくいかもしれない。

sentences.en: Recognizing this possibility does not establish that the person's conclusion is incorrect, but it can provide a reason to examine whether the available alternatives have been considered fairly.
sentences.ja: この可能性を認識しても結論が誤りと確定しないが利用可能な代替案を公平に検討したか調べる理由にはなり得る。

sentences.en: The class consequently avoids treating every personal influence as a logical error while acknowledging that some influences can affect the process through which supporting evidence is selected.
sentences.ja: そこであらゆる個人的影響を論理的誤りと扱わず、一部の影響が根拠選択の過程に作用し得ると認める。

sentences.en: For an exercise, each student writes a short explanation of a position without referring to the identity of the person from whom the idea was originally obtained.
sentences.ja: 練習として各学生は最初に考えを得た人物の身元に言及せず立場の短い説明を書く。

sentences.en: They then identify an objection that would remain worth considering even if it had been raised by someone whose other opinions they strongly disliked.
sentences.ja: 次に他の意見を強く嫌っている人物が述べたとしても検討に値する反論を特定する。

sentences.en: The exercise does not require them to abandon their communities or pretend that their judgments are completely independent of their experiences and relationships.
sentences.ja: 共同体を放棄したり判断が経験や関係から完全に独立していると装ったりすることを練習は要求しない。

sentences.en: Its purpose is to make the grounds for a particular conclusion sufficiently explicit that other people can discuss them without needing to share the same personal history.
sentences.ja: 目的は同じ個人的来歴を共有しなくても他者が議論できるほど特定結論の根拠を明示することだ。

sentences.en: Reasoning becomes a collaborative activity when people are willing to examine the grounds for their beliefs instead of requiring everyone else to reproduce the experiences through which those beliefs were acquired.
sentences.ja: 推論は他者全員に信念獲得の経験を再現させず根拠を検討する意欲があると協働活動になる。

sentences.en: An argument can become stronger when its conclusion is supported by considerations that were not available to the person who first introduced it.
sentences.ja: 論拠は最初の提唱者に利用できなかった考慮事項で結論が支えられると強くなることがある。

sentences.en: Similarly, discovering weaknesses in a familiar argument does not necessarily require rejecting every value associated with the community in which it was learned.
sentences.ja: 同様に慣れた論拠の弱点を発見しても学んだ共同体に関連する全価値を否定する必要は必ずしもない。

sentences.en: For the fictional students, intellectual independence means acquiring the capacity to assess reasons rather than attempting to invent every worthwhile thought entirely on their own.
sentences.ja: 架空学生にとって知的自立とは価値ある全思考を完全に独力で生み出そうとするのでなく理由を評価する能力を得ることを意味する。

not able to be relied on

questions.prompt: What did the students discover about their agreement?
options: They held the same position for different reasons.
They had all copied the same argument.
None could identify their position.
Their instructor had assigned identical reasons.
questions.explanation_ja: 一致する立場と異なる理由。

questions.prompt: What distinction does the instructor invite them to explore?
options: Whether all admired people are specialists.
Whether every belief should be abandoned.
Whether the source of a belief differs from the arguments now supporting it.
Whether debate requires unanimous agreement.
questions.explanation_ja: 信念の来歴と現在の根拠。

questions.prompt: What can happen after encountering an idea through an unreliable source?
options: The idea must remain unjustified forever.
A person may find independent evidence for it.
The person must reject all related ideas.
The original source becomes reliable automatically.
questions.explanation_ja: 独立した根拠を発見可能。

questions.prompt: Why is a respected source not enough to justify continued belief?
options: Specialists are necessarily dishonest.
Respect makes every argument logically false.
A belief has no relationship to circumstances.
The original circumstances supporting the belief may have changed.

questions.prompt: Why does the social history of beliefs still matter?
options: It directly proves which conclusions are true.
It eliminates any need for logical reasoning.
Loyalty may influence how fairly objections are examined.
It guarantees that contrary views are worthless.

questions.prompt: What does the class avoid treating as a logical error automatically?
options: Every personal influence.
A contradiction in reasoning.
All selected evidence.
A specific opposing claim.
questions.explanation_ja: 個人的影響すべてを誤りとしない。

options: A famous person whose name should replace the argument.
An opinion that can never be challenged.
A reason to abandon every community.
An objection worth considering even from a disliked person.
questions.explanation_ja: 相手と独立して反論を検討。

options: So everyone must acquire identical experiences.
So people with different histories can discuss the reasoning.
So personal relationships become irrelevant in all respects.
So no objections can ever arise.
questions.explanation_ja: 異なる背景でも議論可能。

options: Reasons supporting a judgment.
Areas of open land.
Reasons to prohibit an activity.
Members of an institution.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the argument?
options: Every borrowed idea is intellectually worthless.
The origin of a belief alone determines its truth.
Only completely original thoughts can be justified.
Intellectual independence involves assessing reasons while recognizing the social influences on belief.
questions.explanation_ja: 理由の評価と社会的影響の認識。

paraphrases.rewrite: Independence means evaluating reasons, not producing every valuable idea alone.
